mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_ClosedTaskEditRule allows an EditOp to target a Done task with no new_status (or new_status = Done), violating the closed-task reopen invariant from FR-011.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ClosedTaskEditViolation { some e: EditOp | e.target.status = Done and no e.new_status }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AppendOnlyDeletionLog allows two DeletionLog entries to share the same task_ref, violating the append-only, one-entry-per-task invariant from FR-018.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj d1, d2: DeletionLog | d1.task_ref = d2.task_ref }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_DeletedTaskNotEditable allows an EditOp to target a task that is already in the DeletionLog, violating permanent-deletion semantics from FR-012.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DeletedTaskEditable { some e: EditOp | e.target in DeletionLog.task_ref }

mutation_targets.rationale: Replacing F_PermissionMatrix with an empty body allows PermMatrix.Allowed to be any subset, so there could be an OperationKind not allowed for AuthMember, breaking the flat-permissions invariant from FR-003/FR-004.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermMatrixViolation { some op: OperationKind | AuthMember -> op not in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_DeletionLogAttribution allows a DeletionLog entry to have no Member as deleted_by (empty lone field), breaking the attribution invariant from FR-018.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some d: DeletionLog | no m: Member | d.deleted_by = m }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AssigneeIsMember allows a Task.assignee to be set to an atom that is not a Member, violating the workspace-membership requirement for assignees from FR-008.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AssigneeViolation { some t: Task | some t.assignee and t.assignee not in Member }
